findings.statement: REFUTED (round-4's confirmed critical bypass, F-BYPASS-01, is genuinely closed, not relocated): validate_harness.py's forward result->attribution sweep now walks every run directory under .agent-harness/runs/*, not only ACTIVE_RUN. Re-attacked with 4 independent reproductions: (1) a wholly fabricated result dropped into a brand-new, ledger-less, non-legacy-manifest run directory (synthetic fixture); (2) a fabricated result smuggled beside genuinely-ledgered results in a run that has since stopped being ACTIVE_RUN (synthetic fixture, overlapping-run shape); (3) a run directory that is a symlink to a location outside runs/ (Path.glob still follows it; not a silent skip); (4) the same attack executed directly against the REAL, currently-committed bytes of a full clone of this repository at HEAD a3ead1c (not a synthetic fixture): a forged A-R5-FORGED-GHOST.json dropped into the real ledger-less run-20260723-f10-ext01-feasibility-tournament/results/ produces literally zero `git status` output (confirming /.agent-harness/runs/ really is fully gitignored, per .gitignore:62 -- the exact condition that made the original defect invisible), yet validate_harness.py still reports 'Result artifact is not attributed ... A-R5-FORGED-GHOST' and ok:false in every case. All 4 reproductions were caught; none bypassed the sweep.

findings.statement: REFUTED (round-4's other confirmed defect -- last-row-wins ledger / undeclared supersession -- is genuinely closed): check_declared_supersession() in validate_harness.py was attacked with 9 malformed-ledger-row scenarios plus 2 positive controls, all at the unit level (direct calls with crafted row lists, the same technique the shipped test_hooks.py fixtures use) and cross-checked against the existing end-to-end admit_agent.py --reopen tests: (1) reopen row declaring the WRONG superseded digest -- caught; (2) blank reason -- caught; (2b) whitespace-only reason -- caught; (3) event:'minted' masquerading as a reopen (the exact pre-fix laundering shape) -- caught; (4) a genuine 'reopened' row appended AFTER both consume rows (out of causal order) -- caught, i.e. a reopen cannot retroactively license a consume that already happened; (5) a reopen that correctly licenses consume #2 does NOT 'leak forward' to license an undeclared consume #3 -- caught; (6) a reopen row naming a DIFFERENT assignment_id -- caught, does not license this assignment's second consume; (8) reopen row missing the `reason` key entirely -- caught; (9) reopen row missing `superseded_result_sha256` entirely -- caught. Two positive controls (a well-formed single reopen, and two reopens between the same pair of consumes where only the second matches) both correctly produced ZERO false positives, so the check is not over-strict either. Separately, admit_agent.py --reopen against a ledger with a corrupted (non-JSON) line was verified to abort closed (exit 1, 'a reopen must declare the digest it supersedes'), leaving the ledger byte-unchanged and the receipt still 'consumed' rather than minting a reopen row that declares nothing.

findings.statement: REFUTED against the manifest's actual protected state: the legacy-results-manifest laundering channel does not work against the real, currently-committed LEGACY_RESULTS_MANIFEST.json (136 entries, tracked in git; confirmed via `git ls-files`). Two relaunder attempts, run directly against the real committed bytes in the sandbox clone: (A) tampering a REAL legacy-pinned result file's bytes AND editing the committed manifest's digest to match (self-consistent relaunder) -- caught, because the manifest EDIT ITSELF flips `git status` to dirty ('Legacy results manifest modified after commit'), independent of whether the underlying result file is tracked; (B) appending a brand-new blessing entry for a freshly planted, never-before-seen fabricated file -- caught the same way. A DISTINCT, real boundary condition was also confirmed and must be reported precisely: a manifest that has NEVER been committed (this repo's manifest is already committed, so this does not currently apply) tolerates free, undetected edits -- validate_harness.py only appends 'UNCOMMITTED, so the pin is not yet git-bound' to the informational `legacy_results_manifest` status STRING, not to `errors`, so `ok` stays true. This is intentional, shipped-and-tested design (test_legacy_manifest_pins_rather_than_exempts_preadmission_results asserts exactly this), not an oversight, and the SAME manifest becomes fail-closed on its very next edit once it has a single commit to diverge from (independently reproduced here too). Reaching the free-edit window against the real manifest would require first un-tracking an already-committed file (e.g. `git rm --cached`), which is git-history manipulation available only to the same OS user this assignment excludes as a residual, so this is reported as a documented boundary, not a live bypass.
assumptions_used: Un-tracking an already-committed file (git rm --cached, or equivalent index surgery) is treated as within the excluded same-OS-user-forges-artifacts residual, since it requires the same unrestricted local write/execute capability that residual already concedes, applied to .git rather than to a tracked file directly.

findings.statement: CONFIRMED, real gap, needs no forgery at all: the 'open receipt => pending, not error' carve-out gives UNBOUNDED, UN-DIGESTED tolerance for a registered assignment's declared result-file bytes, for as long as its admission receipt is never consumed -- and because round-4's sweep now walks every run directory (not only ACTIVE_RUN), this carve-out's reach is now every run directory, not just the live one. Reproduced with the real, unmodified admit_agent.py (no hand-forged receipt of any kind): mint a receipt for a real, registered assignment in a run that is then made non-active, then overwrite the assignment's declared result path three times in a row with (a) bytes that are not even valid JSON, (b) an unstructured JSON object, and (c) a fabricated RESULT_ENVELOPE-shaped 'pass' with a made-up finding -- validate_harness.py reports ok:true after every single overwrite, with the assignment always listed only under the unscrutinized 'pending_results' array, never digest-checked. This also confirmed the carve-out's intended purpose still works correctly: a genuinely live agent (result written, Stop not yet dispatched) is correctly NOT wedged, in both the active run and a run that has since lost ACTIVE_RUN status (the D-058 overlapping-run shape). Separately, merge_results.py (unrelated to the 4 changed files, read for context) merges every *.json under the active run's results/ into MERGED_RESULTS.json with no admission-state check at all, so a pending, never-Stop-validated result is not just tolerated by the validator but is eligible to be merged as if it were consumed evidence. This does not require the excluded same-OS-user-forgery residual: admit_agent.py is the documented, intended interface, run legitimately; the only 'attack' is choosing not to run Stop. It is bounded by needing the same operator-level trust the whole admission scheme is rooted in (whoever can already run admit_agent.py), not subagent-level access.
assumptions_used: 'Arbitrary bytes' includes non-RESULT_ENVELOPE-shaped and non-JSON content because the pending-results branch in validate_harness.py never calls validate_result_contract() for non-active runs, and does no digest check at all for either active or non-active runs while a receipt stays open.
evidence_refs: .agent-harness/scripts/merge_results.py#L20-L32 (merges every results/*.json with no admission-state check)
counterevidence_refs: docs/audit/BD622_D067_admission_binding_2026-07-29.md#section-2 explicitly names 'a live run wedged by the result<->receipt rule before its Stop is dispatched' as a round-2-fixed defect, so the carve-out's existence is intentional, not accidental; this finding is about its now-global reach and its total lack of any staleness or digest signal, not about its core premise.
unresolved: Whether an open receipt should carry a maximum age / staleness warning, or the pending branch should still require the file to be well-formed JSON, is a design question for the D-070 adjudicator, not decided here.

findings.statement: CONFIRMED but not reachable through normal operation: list_admission_matches() in subagent_start_context.py deliberately folds read/parse failures for EVERY receipt file in the run's admissions dir into the result, not only ones that happen to match the querying agent_id (this is explicit, documented behavior: 'an unprovable negative must not default to PASS'). Reproduced: a single corrupted (non-JSON) receipt file for assignment B hard-fails SubagentStart ('Hook preflight: FAIL') for a THIRD agent that was never registered for any assignment at all and has nothing to do with assignment B -- confirming the blast radius is the whole run, not the affected assignment. This self-heals immediately: removing the corrupt file restores normal Start behavior for every agent on the next invocation (no persistent wedge, no state to clean up beyond the bad file itself). Also confirmed: (i) Start never mutates .agent-harness/admissions/ under this or any other scenario tested (receipt bytes and directory listing byte-identical before/after, across all 8 fixture scenarios and this DOS probe); (ii) 4 threads hammering SubagentStart concurrently against 15 sequential admit_agent.py mint/--reopen calls for 30+ seconds produced zero torn/partial receipt reads, consistent with dump_json_atomic's write-temp+os.replace pattern. Verdict is 'inconclusive' rather than 'fail' because the only way a receipt becomes corrupted under the atomic-write scheme this mechanism actually uses is the excluded same-OS-user-forges-artifacts residual; under normal operation (including concurrent admits) no torn or corrupted receipt was produced.
evidence_refs: .codex/hooks/subagent_start_context.py#L1-L59 (module docstring: 'Ambiguity is a FAIL, not a skip')
counterevidence_refs: The corrupt-receipt-blocks-unrelated-agent behavior matches the module's own stated design intent verbatim, so it is not an unintended defect of the round-4 fix pass.
unresolved: Whether the blast radius (whole run vs. only the affected assignment_id) is the intended tradeoff or should be narrowed is a design question, not a bug found here.

findings.statement: Incidental finding, confirmed PRE-EXISTING and NOT introduced by the round-4 fix pass, reported for completeness only: validate_harness.py's main() crashes with an unhandled Python traceback (FileNotFoundError reading RUN_PLAN.json), rather than the intended graceful `{"ok": false, "errors": [...]}` JSON, when ACTIVE_RUN names a run_id whose directory does not exist on disk at all (as opposed to being present but malformed, which is handled). `git log -p --follow` on validate_harness.py shows the unconditional `run_dir / "RUN_PLAN.json"` load at the top of the `if active:` block was already present, unchanged, at commit a1cdd8a (the pre-fix baseline for this round), so this is not a regression this round's fix pass could have introduced and is out of the stated scope (hunting what round 4 broke). Verdict is 'inconclusive' rather than 'fail' to avoid conflating a real-but-unrelated, pre-existing robustness gap with the round-4 regression hunt this assignment asks for.
assumptions_used: An ACTIVE_RUN file naming a genuinely nonexistent run directory is itself an unusual/degraded state (normally init_run.py creates the run atomically before ACTIVE_RUN is ever pointed at it), so this is reported as a minor robustness observation, not a security finding.
counterevidence_refs: git show a1cdd8a:.agent-harness/scripts/validate_harness.py already contains the identical unconditional RUN_PLAN.json load, confirming this predates the round-4 fix pass under review.
reproduction: git log -p --follow -- .agent-harness/scripts/validate_harness.py | grep -n 'run_dir / "RUN_PLAN.json"'   # present since before a1cdd8a
unresolved: Whether this pre-existing crash-vs-graceful-error gap is worth a follow-up fix is a call for whoever owns the harness backlog next; it is out of this round's scope.
